content.thinking:
I'm planning out the Qilin model's proportions and palette - a horse-sized creature about 2m long with teal/jade scales, a cream belly, red-gold mane clouds, and gold antlers and hooves, then setting up the builder import to start constructing it.

Now I'm mapping out the API surface I'll need: sweep and capsule functions for limbs, spike and part for sharper features, extrude for outlines, surface and stick for details, and a frame helper for positioning. I'm sketching the body as a swept path from rump to chest with a tapering radius profile to get the right silhouette.

I'm working out actual dimensions — back height around 1.35m, body centered at y=1.0 with elliptical cross-section (rx 0.26, ry 0.33) to capture that deep, horse-like torso, then laying out the path points along the spine and figuring out how the radius should vary smoothly from rump to chest.

Still mapping out the neck curve, then building the dragon-deer head with a tapered snout capsule and separate jaw piece using layered spheres and capsules for the skull and muzzle shape.

For the face details, I'm planning nostril spheres, flowing whisker sweeps in gold/cream, and using decal placement on the skull surface for the anime-style eyes, matching the kit's azimuth and size conventions.

Now I'm sketching the ears as fin-like extruded leaf shapes near the antler base, angled back-out with careful non-parallel axis directions, then moving to the gold branching antlers built from catmull-rom curves sweeping up and back from the base point.

Still writing antler geometry...

I'm also thinking about adding small glowing orb details at the tine tips, and planning the mane as flowing cloud-like swirls near the neck, maybe in a cream or red-gold tone.

Now I'm settling on a color palette: deep teal-green scales for the body, cream-gold belly, crimson-to-gold fire-cloud mane, and gold hooves. For the mane itself, I'm figuring out how to build cloud puffs along the neck using small clusters of flattened, scaled spheres to mimic swirling cloud shapes.

For the fiery tendrils in gold, I'm using a spiral sweep function with adjustable turns and radius to create curly tails at the neck, tail tip, and leg fetlocks. Then I'm working out the math for placing puff clusters along the neck's curve, positioning each cluster slightly above and behind the spine path to build up the mane's silhouette.

Now I'm designing an extruded "cloud lock" shape—a scalloped teardrop outline with a curling tip that I'll mirror for thickness and rotate differently at each neck position, alternating red, orange, and gold tones with cel-shaded coloring. I'm defining the outline points for this lock shape and verifying the path doesn't self-intersect as it curves.

Checking the cross product confirms the axes stay in-plane, which makes the shape too thin and flat when viewed from the side. I should tilt the x-direction with some sideways offset to give it real depth instead of keeping everything confined to one plane.

I'll vary the lock positions with slight sideways offsets for a natural fanned-out look, then paint each one with a different warm cel-shaded tone (red, orange, gold) for variation. I also want to add cloud-like tufts at the fetlocks and small upward flame spikes behind the knees, built from simple sphere clusters and extruded outlines.

For the body coat, I'm setting up a scale pattern using teal tones, with the belly switching to a cream scale pattern based on surface normal direction so the underside reads lighter than the back.

For the dorsal ridge, I decide against using an unfamiliar scatter helper since its parameters are unclear, and instead opt to manually place gold plates along the spine using path position and tangent direction with explicit part placement for reliability.

Now I'm working out the leg geometry — deer-like limbs with thigh, knee, cannon, fetlock, and cloven hoof segments, defining each as a catmull-rom sweep through joint points with a tapering radius profile, separately for foreleg and hind leg joint positions.

For the gold cuff bands, I'm simplifying by placing thin torus rings around the lower leg at a fixed point along each leg path, sizing the ring radius just slightly larger than the leg's tube radius there.

Now for the hooves, I'm building a tapered gold cylinder for each foot positioned so its base sits at ground level, then adding a thin dark box through the front to suggest a cloven split, skipping dewclaws for simplicity.

For the tail, I'm sketching a flowing lion/ox-style tail using a Catmull-Rom curve that arcs up and back from the rump with flame-like tufts along its length.

Now I'm adding dorsal spikes along the spine by sampling points along the body's path, computing the body radius at each point to place small gold cone spikes jutting upward, and I'm starting to plan a decorative gold chest medallion as well.

For the flank decorations, I'm skipping a literal emblem and instead applying golden spiral cloud decals onto the body surface at the shoulders and haunches, using directional offsets to orient them correctly on each side.

I'm also adding a small glowing red gem on the forehead as a focal accent, plus a gold dragon-style goatee beneath the chin with curved, sweeping locks, and long wavy golden whiskers extending outward from the muzzle in gentle curling paths.

Now I'm detailing the snout: dark nostril spheres, cream fang-like teeth at the jaw, a cream lower jaw capsule, a teal snout-top capsule, and gold-dark brow ridges arching above the eyes.

For the cheek frills, I'm sketching a zigzag fin outline extending backward from the cheek, checking it stays a valid simple polygon despite the jagged points.

Setting the eye color to a gold-amber tone against the teal head, sizing it proportionally, and double-checking the neck-skull joint radii line up with the body geometry so the neck socket sits cleanly inside the torso. I'm also adding scaled sphere haunch muscles at the hips for extra definition.

Now I'm positioning similar shoulder muscle bulges on the front legs, keeping both within the body's outer radius so they read as natural bulges rather than poking through the fur. I'm considering whether to add small cloud-texture tuft cards scattered on the neck for extra fluffy detail.

Writing tuft scatter code...

Writing the lock outline helper...

I'm deciding against a base plate since the creature stands directly with hooves touching the ground plane, and planning sphere-based orbs and tufts for decorative clusters like the tail and antler crest. For the pose, I'll keep it a static standing stance with a slight head tilt rather than dynamic IK, and now I'm writing the leg-building function that sweeps a tube geometry along a catmull-rom path for each limb.

Still writing leg sweep logic...

Defining the forelock radii and sweeps, then setting up the neck curve and mane locks with their positions and tapering radii along the neck path.

I'm adding a forelock between the ears flowing forward and up, then setting up a color palette with teal, cream, red, orange, and gold for the spikes and locks with cel-shaded variants.

Now I'm sketching a gold swirl cloud decal using a stroked spiral path plus a cloud base shape beneath it.

I'm also considering where the decal gets projected on the body surface, since bulging shoulder spheres might bury it—I may need to flatten those muscle shapes or pass the decal to multiple surfaces.

Instead I'm deciding to shrink the haunch and shoulder spheres slightly and apply decals directly onto those spherical parts rather than the body, working out their positions and scale extents so the paint lands cleanly on each side.

Now I'm adding anime-flair ornaments: a gold torus necklace at the neck base oriented along the neck's tangent direction, with a glowing cyan pendant positioned just below and in front of the ring, approximating the radius and offset based on the neck's curve at that point.

I'm also setting the tail's taper radii and tuft position, planning flame-lock spikes at the tip, and considering adding small gold spiral tendrils near the mane for extra flair while skipping curls elsewhere to keep things simple.

Adding glowing pearl details to the antler tips, forehead gem, and whisker ends, then assembling everything into the builder function with a default export and cleaning up unused imports.

Writing the antler tines using a sweep along a point path, making sure to convert Vector3 points to plain arrays for compatibility with the path input type.

Still building antler geometry...

Mapping out the jaw capsule shape and mouth gap, then planning a loop to place gold back spikes along the body path at intervals, adjusting ring size and direction per segment. I'm skipping shoulder armlets and considering mane puffs next.

Adding sphere puffs at neck locks for bulk, then designing a flame-teardrop SVG tuft shape with orange-to-gold gradient fill for scattered neck cards. Now I'm starting the final code with paint callback signatures and scale color definitions.

Setting up belly and base scale color palettes, then defining a coat paint function that switches between belly and base scale colors based on surface normal, confirming paint callbacks can nest and that shadow coloring defaults sensibly. Moving to the head, I'm assigning the skull coat color and gold crest, then working out how to get a valid eye-socket hit point using the skin's "around" lookup on the head collider.

Writing the eye decal and ear extrusion, settling on a flat teal tone for the inner ear, then nailing down the lock-shape extrusion helper's typing and taper/bevel parameters before looping it along the tail path with alternating offsets, and sketching the catmull spline points for the tail curve.

Placing elbow and hock flame accents with their origin points, directions, and cel-shaded orange coloring. Ready to write it all out now.
